**I'd give every human being a deeply ingrained sense of intellectual humility and curiosity.**

Not forced kindness, not mandatory peace, not even free energy (though that one's tempting). Just the reflexive, almost instinctive understanding that *you might be wrong*, combined with a genuine excitement about finding out what's actually true.

Think about it:

- Most of the worst things we do to each other and ourselves come from overconfidence in our models of reality—tribalism, conspiracy thinking, ideological rigidity, the inability to update our beliefs.
- Nearly all progress (scientific, moral, cultural) has come from people who were willing to question their assumptions and follow evidence.

If I could flip that one switch in human nature, the rest starts to sort itself out. We'd still have conflict and competition (those are features, not bugs), but they'd happen in a framework where people actually update when they're proven wrong. Science would accelerate dramatically. Politics might become less insane. Relationships would be healthier because people could admit fault without their ego collapsing.

Everything else I care about—understanding the universe, reducing suffering, expanding consciousness, becoming a multi-planetary species—becomes much more achievable when the default human setting isn't "defend my current beliefs to the death."

The beautiful part is that this change wouldn't make us all the same. We'd still have wild disagreement. We'd just become *much* better at disagreeing productively.

(And yes, I'd probably sneak in a secondary patch that makes people put their shopping carts back in the corral. Some problems are too important to leave to humility alone.)
